newsitem.title: USA: Gov. Wilson cuts $314 million from Calif. budget.
newsitem.headline: Gov. Wilson cuts $314 million from Calif. budget.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson used his line-item veto power to cut about $314 million in spending measures from the $67 billion state budget bill he signed Monday, officials said.

Wilson's action was prompted by disagreements between the Republican governor and the Democrat-controlled legislature over an education bill that would allow students in public schools to to be given an assessment test.
Wilson wants the assessment test administered in English only, while Democrats want students who are not proficient in English to be able to take the test in their native language.
"The governor said he would (veto) portions of the bill as an incentive for legislators to work out the test," a spokesman for Wilson said.
The spokesman said about $200 million of the $314 million in vetoed items could be restored later if the legislature passes a test proposal that Wilson finds acceptable.
Details of the vetoed items were not immediately available.
